A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H-embedding-guided hypernetwork research. All 20 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original continual-learning comparisons and ablations on PermutedMNIST, CIFAR10/100, and ImageNet-R, including detailed per-task results in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds LoRA, DomainNet, class-incremental, ablation, and timing results. Some comparator scores are explicitly attributed to previous work.

M1.justification: The H-embedding construction and guidance losses remain essentially unchanged. V2 adds LoRA-only parameter generation with a frozen pretrained backbone (Section 4.2.3), plus a class-incremental inference procedure using a classifier trained on cached frozen-model features to select task embeddings (Section 5.3).

E1.justification: V2 adds pooled DomainNet data and evaluates ImageNet-R without supplied task IDs through a class-incremental extension. It replaces the eleven-task CIFAR10/100 benchmark with ten-task CIFAR-100, dropping the initial CIFAR-10 task. PermutedMNIST remains in the appendix.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-Prompt, HiDe-Prompt, InfLoRA, and SD-LoRA comparisons under ViT-B/16. Finetune Head and Multi Task disappear from the earlier comparison; Finetune is retained as Full Finetune. The original full-generation ablation comparators remain in Appendix A.6.

E3.justification: V2 introduces pretrained ViT-B/16 evaluation, LoRA training budgets, five- and twenty-task ImageNet-R partitions, and testing with inferred task IDs. It also changes the reported CIFAR sequence and foregrounds FAA/DAA while redefining BWT/FWT. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds component ablations removing H-embedding guidance, CL regularization, and AHP normalization across three sequence lengths, plus inference-time measurements and a class-incremental trial. Earlier full-generation ablations and convergence/embedding analyses remain in the appendix, with adjustments for CIFAR-100.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging, seeds 22/32/42, and accuracy standard deviations remain documented. However, v2 Table 6 omits the BWT/FWT standard deviations reported in v1 Table 1, removes per-task uncertainty tables, and drops v1's explicit disclosure that ablations used single runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results, including LoRA FAA of 97.07 on CIFAR-100, 81.38 on ten-task ImageNet-R, and 76.64 on DomainNet. CIFAR accuracy changes from 83.58 to 83.08 alongside revised task coverage; the ResNet ImageNet-R accuracy of 38.16 remains unchanged. V1's detailed per-task result matrices are removed.

T1.justification: The H-score/AHP mathematics and Appendix A.2 argument are retained. V2 Section 5.3 substantively changes the formal transfer definitions to BWT = FAA - DAA and FWT = DAA - GTA, replacing v1's averages that excluded the last or first task and used denominator M-1.

C1.justification: The central claim that transferability-aware embeddings improve continual learning through hypernetwork guidance remains. V2 adds an explicit introductory contribution concerning plug-in generation of components such as LoRA and compatibility with pretrained models; the principal novelty and overall performance claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of amortized inference cost and parameter efficiency, interprets sequence-length results as evidence of robustness, and acknowledges that its CIL extension depends on pretrained features and a separately trained classifier that fits imperfectly with online learning. Earlier convergence and embedding interpretations largely move to Appendix A.7.

D1.justification: V2 documents LoRA rank/alpha 16, dropout 0.1, generated parameter counts, training budgets, and additional benchmark hyperparameters. It newly specifies a two-layer decoder and weight chunks of size 7000. These disclosures do not establish changes to the earlier implementation. The code-access URL is retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around pretrained models, prompting, and LoRA-based continual learning, adding the associated comparison literature and ViT/DomainNet references. The introduction also develops a prior-versus-posterior task-relation distinction, including new discussion of Riemer et al.; earlier rehearsal-free background is retained in the appendix.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction and experimental narrative, presents H-embedding before the hypernetwork framework, moves hypernetwork background into the preliminaries, and reorganizes supplementary material. Existing performance analyses move to the appendix, and the author block changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Table 1 is redesigned around backbone groups and FAA/DAA, and new comparison and ablation displays are added. V1 Figures 1 and 4 and its detailed per-task tables disappear; convergence plots and the embedding heatmap are relocated and adjusted.

improvement.justification: New component ablations, LoRA/CIL tests, and timing measurements strengthen support for design choices and practical applicability. The gain is limited by removal of v1's per-task results and transfer uncertainties, and by a new reporting overstatement: v2 Table 5 claims the highest DAA throughout, although CIFAR-100 DAA is 76.900 for the proposed method versus 79.490 for Vanilla Hnet.
